Attached: dpa-redline-v3.docx (redlines from our counsel) and a simple data-flow diagram for reference. Can you confirm whether any default subprocessor locations are outside the continental US? We flagged potential compliance concerns for Oregon and California jurisdictions.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Tara Bell <tara.bell@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed CPRA service-provider clause and sale carve-out

Tara / Logan — please find below proposed language (inline) for the addendum. This is intended to be CPRA-aligned and minimize back-and-forth. Feel free to pull into your redline doc.

Proposed clause (clean):
"Redwood Inference shall be deemed a 'service provider' under the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA) with respect to Personal Information Processed on Customer's behalf. Redwood shall not 'sell' Personal Information, nor shall Redwood knowingly facilitate the sale of Personal Information, and any use of Personal Information for purposes of providing the services (including analytics used to operate, debug, or improve service quality) is limited to performing the contract, security, fraud prevention, and service optimization. Such uses do not constitute a 'sale' under the CPRA. Redwood will not combine Customer Personal Information with information purchased from third parties for the purposes of targeted advertising.

Subprocessors and transfers: Redwood will maintain a list of subprocessors and their geographic locations. For the avoidance of doubt, Redwood shall not transfer Customer Personal Information outside the continental United States except (i) where necessary to provide the Service and (ii) with Customer's prior written consent or where Customer has elected a region that includes the destination. Where transfers occur, Redwood will ensure appropriate contractual and technical safeguards consistent with US state privacy obligations and will document the transfer in the transfer matrix.

If Acme wants an explicit sentence about 'no sale via targeted advertising' I can add one; current language attempts to be consistent with industry practice and avoids conflicting with service operation clauses.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
"

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tara Bell <tara.bell@acmeretail.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 14:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Data-flow / subprocessor note (technical)

Tara — quick technical note to accompany Neha's language. Per the diagram, artifacts produced by inference (generated text, embeddings, logs) follow these paths:
- Real-time inference tokens: processed on the serving runtime in the customer-designated region. No default replication outside region unless customer enables cross-region backup.
- Aggregated telemetry (service metrics, token counts): periodically sent to central metrics pipeline in us-west-2 for billing and platform health. These metrics are pseudonymized and do not include raw customer texts.
- Subprocessors: current default list for hosted accounts is: GPU hosting partner (us-west-2), metrics/observability provider (us-west-2), payments processor (us-east-1), and an optional partner for embeddings index storage (us-west-2). None are located in APAC/EU by default for this account. If Acme chooses a dedicated region or private deployment, the topology changes and we will provide a dedicated subprocessor map.

I'll attach a concise transfer matrix (see attachment: data-flow-diagram.png) and can draw a table for procurement if needed.

— Karthik
Staff Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

We are comfortable to proceed with the DPA once those two points are inserted and the minor redlines in the attached doc are reconciled. Can we get a final redline by COB 10/2? We can then route through DocuSign.
